newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt seeks to reverse slide in Suez Canal revenue.
newsitem.headline: Egypt seeks to reverse slide in Suez Canal revenue.

text.p: Egypt's Suez Canal Authority (SCA) is trying to reverse a slide in revenues, a vital foreign currency source, by making the canal more competitive and encouraging oil shipping traffic, officials said on Monday.

Officials from the Egyptian parliament's transportation committee and the Suez Canal Authority met to discuss the reasons behind the decline in revenues, which fell by more than $100 million in the nine-month period January-September 1996.
The canal earned $1.45 billion in the same period of 1995.

Suez Canal Authority chairman Ahmed Fadel said the authority was working to make canal transit time and fees more competitive and there were "continous contacts" between the authority and oil exporters to use the canal.

The canal, facing competition from the SUMED pipeline, which pumps crude oil from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean, and from the Cape route around Africa's southern tip, is fighting hard to win back traffic.
The SCA and the company that runs the pipeline decided earlier to form a committee to coordinate boosting traffic.
Fadel said organisation and cooperation with SUMED "has not yet been implemented".
He asked the parliamentary committee to review privileges granted to SUMED and to stop it accepting oil from vessels which could pass through the canal.
Suez Canal officials have said they are worried about SUMED's expansion of the pipeline's pumping capacity to 117 million tonnes of oil a year.
Competition from SUMED reduced Suez Canal revenue by $47 million in the past five months of 1996 compared to the same period last year, one canal official said.
The fall in revenue followed sharp cuts in fees announced by SCA last year for some crude oil tankers transiting the canal in a bid to win back traffic from the pipeline.

SUMED, which is 50 percent owned by the Egyptian government, runs across Egypt from Ain Sukhna at the head of the Gulf of Suez to a terminal on the Mediterranean. The other SUMED shareholders are Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.
